Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said, 50 crore Indians have escaped extreme poverty over the past 12 years. Addressing the jawans on the occasion of Diwali in Bastar, Chhattisgarh yesterday, Prime Minister compared India’s welfare architecture over the past 12 years to a Diwali Rangoli where small, distinct lines come together to form a grand picture.

Prime Minister Modi said, the poor families whose entire lives used to be spent only in worry have now received the assurance of the government, and a new self-confidence has come into them.

The Prime Minister detailed the special development drive in Left-Wing Extremism-affected areas that built over 15,000 kilometers of roads, over 9,500 mobile towers, nearly 175 Eklavya schools, around 50 ITIs, 50 Skill Development Centres, and thousands of post offices, bank branches, and ATMs, alongside rehabilitating surrendered Naxals and bringing water, electricity, and roads to remote tribal villages for the first time under PM JANMAN.

Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah will inaugurate and lay the foundation stone for various development projects worth 1,024 crore rupees in Ahmedabad, Gujarat today. A Report:

“Union Minister Amit Shah will dedicate and lay the foundation stone for a total of 30 development projects worth 1,024 crore rupees in his Gandhinagar Lok Sabha constituency. These projects primarily include various civic amenities by the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation, such as housing and water supply schemes. His schedule will begin with the inauguration of the four-kilometer-long flyover stretching from ISKCON to Sanand on the SG Highway. Following this, he will inaugurate a newly built Knowledge Hub and dedicate an Urban Health Centre in city. He will also visit the housing scheme units in Vadaj. Concluding his itinerary, Mr. Shah will attend a public event in Ranip, where he will also conduct the draw for the housing scheme beneficiaries. Harshal Pandya Akashvani News, Ahmedabad.”

National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) capped trade margins on MRP of 137 anti-cancer drugs, based on the recommendations of Expert Committee constituted by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) under Ministry of Health & Family Welfare. The revised prices of these drugs come into effect from today. As on date, 76 pharmaceutical companies have reported revised MRP for 1225 anti-cancer formulations, covering 121 drugs. Reduction in the MRP have been reported in 1031 formulations of anti-cancer medicines, with 600 brands reporting above 50 percent reduction and the highest reduction being 96.45 percent. Further, out of the 137 identified anti-cancer drugs, there are 10-15 drugs which are yet to be launched in India. However, Trade Margin Rationalization (TMR) will be applicable on these drugs also as and when they are launched.  As a result of the price reductions to be effected from today, the estimated annual savings to consumers would be 3,502.31 crore rupees.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has extended his greetings to the people of Uttarakhand on the occasion of its Foundation Day. In a social media post, the Prime Minister described Uttarakhand as a divine land rich in spiritual consciousness and breathtaking natural beauty. He noted that the state, with its picturesque mountain landscapes, sacred rivers and the holy Char Dham, also has a distinct identity rooted in its cultural heritage.

Nineteen Indian seafarers stranded in Yemen’s Hodeidah and Sana’a for the past two weeks have been evacuated, with all of them safe and on their way back to their country. The Indian Embassy in Yemen yesterday said, all seafarers are safe, in good health, and on their way back to India. In a social media post, the Embassy thanked all concerned for their valuable cooperation and continued support in facilitating the safe evacuation of the stranded Indian nationals.

Leaders, scientists, civil society representatives, activists and others from nearly 200 countries, including India, are gathering for two weeks in Turkey’s Mediterranean resort city of Antalya for the 31st Conference of Parties to the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), beginning today, with aim to accelerate clean energy, scale up climate finance and strengthen resilience. The summit will continue till November 20.

The Conference of the Parties (COP), the highest-level global climate summit held annually under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), is bringing together heads of state, Ministers, scientists, business leaders, and civil society representatives from around the world and serves as the primary platform for negotiating and advancing collective action to combat climate change. At COP31, the World Metrological Organisation (WMO) will support countries by providing authoritative scientific observations and information on the state of the global climate system, including through the launch of its flagship State of Climate update 2026, a science-based annual assessment of climate indicators and impacts.

Israeli President Isaac Herzog yesterday formally tasked Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a government after he secured recommendations from 67 of the 120 elected members of the parliament, compared with 46 for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Eisenkot, a former chief of the Israel Defence Forces (IDF), has 28 days to form a government and secure the approval of the Knesset — Israel’s parliament. He may seek an additional 14-day extension from Herzog for government formation.

The October 27 elections, seen as a referendum on Netanyahu’s leadership, produced no clear majority but divided the political landscape into two competing blocs, with the anti-Netanyahu alliance recommending Eisenkot.

National Entrepreneurship Day is being observed today. The day highlights the importance of entrepreneurship in India’s development journey. The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship was also established on this day in 2014. With over 2.62 lakh Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade-recognised startups, India has emerged as the world’s third largest startup ecosystem, creating employment and expanding opportunities for its youth. A report:

“Over the past decade, youth have increasingly moved beyond the role of beneficiaries to become active contributors to national development. The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship has informed that startups have been able to create more than 23 lakh jobs till March this year. The Government has recognized over 55 thousand 200 startups during 2025-26 which is the highest number of startups recognized in a single year since 2016. Along with this, more than 1 lakh recognized startups have at least one woman director or partner. Government initiatives like Startup India, Atal Innovation Mission, Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology Startup Hub, Technology Incubation and Development of Entrepreneurs (TIDE) 2.0 Scheme, Gen-Next Support for Innovative Startups initiative, National Initiative for Developing and Harnessing Innovations, Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme and Swavalambini Scheme have supported innovation, easier access to finance, digital platforms, mentorship and enterprise creation. Their expanding contribution reflects India’s growing entrepreneurial capacity and the potential of innovation-led enterprises to support long-term, inclusive development. Saumya Sharan for Akashvani News, Delhi.”

A day after Diwali, a thick blanket of smog engulfed several parts of Delhi this morning, as air quality in the national capital continued to remain in the ‘Very Poor’ category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi recorded an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 368 at 7 AM today. The smog also led to a significant reduction in visibility across several parts of the city.

The air quality remained poor despite the Supreme Court allowing only the bursting of green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR during fixed hours on 7th and 8th of November.

China’s Xiao Jiaruixuan won gold while Hungary’s Veronika Major claimed silver. India’s Manvi Jain and Simranpreet Kaur Brar finished eighth and 10th, respectively.

The festival of light Deepawali is being celebrated with religious fervour and gaiety across the country and abroad. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will continue his tradition of celebrating Diwali with the brave personnel of the Armed Forces. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has also greeted everyone on the occasion of Diwali. In a social media post this morning, the Prime Minister said, the festival symbolises resolve against darkness. Prime Minister Modi also shared a video message on social media. He said, the festival of lights illuminates the nation and reflects the resolve to overcome darkness. He wished everyone happiness, peace and prosperity.

 

President Droupadi Murmu has extended Diwali greetings to Indians at home and abroad. In her message, she said the festival symbolises the victory of virtue over negativity and marks the end of suffering and the beginning of a joyful and prosperous life. The President has also urged people to protect the environment, promote harmony and contribute towards building a Viksit Bharat.

In Uttar Pradesh, festival of lights Diwali is being celebrated with religious fervour and zeal. More from our correspondent:

 

“Pilgrims are taking dip in holy mandakini river in Chitrakoot where according to mythology Lord Rama spent a lot of time during his vanvas. Major buildings and temple are decorated with lights. Preparation for Lakshmi pooja is in full swing and rangolis will be made to welcome goddess of wealth. Yesterday Yogi government celebrated a grand Deepotsav in Ayodhya in which vice president CP Radhakrishnan attended the function as chief guest. More than 30 lakh earthen lamps were eliminated on the 56 ghats of rivers Saryu. Today Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will celebrate diwali with Vantangiya community. Chief Minister will launch 52 development projects worth 82 crore rupees for the Vantangia people living in the deep dark forest of Gorakhpur district. He has been celebrating diwali since decades with these tribal people living in the forests of Gorakhpur and neighbouring areas. Chife Minster will later perform Deepdan in Gorakhnath temple. Sushil Chandra tiwari, AKASHvANI NEWS, Lucknow.”

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has urged the armed forces to maintain the highest level of operational readiness, stressing the need to strengthen domain awareness, cyber resilience and information integrity amid evolving security challenges.

 

Addressing Indian Air Force (IAF) personnel at Air Force Station Bagdogra in West Bengal on the eve of Diwali, Mr Singh said, modern warfare has expanded beyond conventional border conflicts to include asymmetric warfare, proxy conflicts, cyberattacks, drone swarms and information operations.

 

The Defence Minister emphasised that military personnel must play a wider role in countering such threats by maintaining public trust and engaging with local communities.

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will visit Sikkim this morning to celebrate Diwali with the troops deployed along the Indo-China border. The Defence Minister will visit Sherathang War Memorial near Nathula to pay homage to the brave soldiers who laid down their lives for the nation. Mr Singh will also interact with the defence personnel deployed in the area. More from our Correspondent:

 

 

”In a short while from now, Raksha Mantri Rajnath Singh will arrive at Sherathang War Memorial which is also known as the Watershed Martyr’s Memorial. Sherathang War Memorial is located at the altitude of over 13 thousand feet near the Nathula Pass. It was built to honour the brave Indian Army martyrs and heroes of the 1967 Nathula and Cho La clashes against the Chinese force. Raksha Mantri will also interact with the soldiers deployed. Senior army officers and Sikkim government officials will accompany the Union Minister during this visit. manas pratima sharma, akashvani news, nathula”

In West Bengal, Shyama Puja, popularly known as Kali Puja, is being celebrated today across West Bengal and several parts of the country with traditional fervour and devotion. The festival coincides with Diwali in many parts of the country. Our Kolkata Correspondent reports, as darkness descends on the new moon night, Bengal lights up in a spectacular celebration of faith, devotion and artistry.

 

The festival is observed on the new moon night of the Hindu month of Kartik, following traditional rituals and religious customs. Some of Bengal’s most revered Kali temples are witnessing special arrangements for the occasion. The Dakshineswar Bhavatarini Temple, closely associated with the spiritual legacy of Sri Ramakrishna Paramahansa, the historic Kalighat Kali Temple, Tarapith and Adyapeath are among the major centres of attraction. The historic Hanseswari Temple at Bansberia in Hooghly district, the famous Boro Maa Kali Puja in Naihati and the Kali temple at Kankalitala, one of the revered Shakti Peethas, are also preparing to receive large numbers of devotees. As Bengal celebrates the triumph of divine power over evil, the night of Amavasya is transformed into a celebration of light, faith and devotion. Sandipon Dasgupta, akashvani news, Kolkata.”

The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas has reaffirmed the claim that E20 petrol supplied by public sector oil marketing companies (OMCs) across the country, including Karnataka, conforms to the prescribed quality standards. It noted that E20 petrol supplied by the three OMCs conforms to IS 17021, the Bureau of Indian Standards specification for ethanol-blended motor gasoline. The Ministry rejected the claims of Karnataka Government that fuel sold at certain retail outlets in the state contains excessive ethanol. We have a Report :

 

                                               

“The Ministry said that 893 samples collected across 27 States and Union Territories, including 56 from Karnataka, meet the prescribed specifications. The Ministry added that all 56 samples tested in Karnataka conform to IS 17021 specifications, with ethanol content ranging from 19 to 20 per cent. Earlier, the three oil marketing companies, Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum Corporation and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation, had clarified that the claims, as reported, were not supported by tests conducted in accordance with the prescribed statutory and technical procedures. With VISHNU AND ANAND, ANUPAM MISHRA, AKASHVANI NEWS, DELHI.”

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said, Lal Krishna Advani gave the Bharatiya Janata Party BJP a clear foundation rooted in the principle of Nation First. Paying tributes through articles in leading dailies to the former Deputy Prime Minister and BJP patriarch who turns 99 today, Mr Modi said, two qualities set Mr Advani apart as a leader, his ideological clarity and intellectual sharpness, and the manner in which he challenged the pseudo-secularism propounded by a large section of the political class for years. Mr Modi credited Mr Advani’s tenures as BJP president with the Congress falling sharply from 400 seats to below 200 in 1989 and the emerging as the single largest party for the first time in 1996. Recalling the 1991 Lok Sabha elections, Mr Modi said, Mr Advani contested from two seats, one of them was Gandhinagar. The Prime Minister said, he had helped prepare Mr Advani’s nomination papers and assisted in the campaign.

The US Central Command (CENTCOM) has announced the establishment of a new task force aimed at disrupting Iran’s alleged use of land-based transit routes to transport advanced weapons, as Washington intensifies efforts to curb Tehran’s military supply networks. We have a report:

 

“The CENTCOM said in a statement that the ‘Task Force Iron Gate will comprise approximately 20 civilian and military personnel based in Tampa, Florida. It will coordinate with various US government agencies to prevent the movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials and illicit revenue streams across Iran’s land borders and the Caspian Sea. CENTCOM also claimed that the US naval blockade had prevented Iran from exporting more than 25 billion dollar worth of crude oil in recent months. The announcement comes amid statements by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Aerospace Force highlighting the country’s domestic defence manufacturing capabilities, technological advancements and commitment to military self-reliance. With vikas sharma’s report, Yashasvi Kiryal, AKASHVANI NEWS DELHI.”

In Poland, six people were killed and 15 wounded after a gunman opened fire yesterday in a busy market square in Krakow. The gunman, a Polish citizen, aimed at random people as he drove into the Main Square, a major tourist destination in the centre of the city, Krakow police said. Police officers are among the wounded. The perpetrator was shot and wounded during a gunfight with officers a short distance away from the initial violence, police said. Katarzyna Cislo, a spokesperson for the Krakow police, told reporters that the perpetrator was wearing military-style fatigues and he used a military-type long gun in the attack.

A strong earthquake shook central Japan early in the morning, shattering store windows, causing people to flee buildings and leaving at least 22 people injured. Japan’s Meteorological Agency put the quake’s magnitude at 5.7, while the US Geological Survey reported it at magnitude 5.5. Smaller aftershocks were also reported. Japan is located in an area that is prone to earthquakes.

Electronics and Information Technology Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw has said, India remains focused on becoming the artificial intelligence (AI) “application capital” of the world. Speaking to the media in New Delhi yesterday, Mr. Vaishnaw said the country is working towards expanding the use of  Artificial Intelligence across key sectors, including agriculture, healthcare and education. He added that Indian industries are making significant progress in developing AI-based applications.

 

Responding to questions on the recent global fall in technology stocks amid concerns over the future of AI investments, Mr. Vaishnaw said the AI industry is undergoing a period of rapid change and uncertainty. He said India is focusing on expanding the use of AI across various sectors and developing applications that can bring large-scale transformation.

India and the European Union have successfully concluded negotiations on New Delhi’s association with Horizon Europe, the bloc’s 93.5-billion-euro flagship research and innovation funding programme. Under the arrangement, Indian researchers, businesses and research organisations will be eligible to receive direct funding from Horizon Europe and lead international collaborative research projects under its second pillar, which focuses on global challenges and European industrial competitiveness. Once signed and ratified by both sides, the agreement is expected to come into effect in January next year.

 

“The Horizon Europe programme covers key areas such as healthcare, artificial intelligence, digital technology, space, climate, energy and industrial development. The European Commission said the agreement marks a significant milestone in India-EU relations and will strengthen scientific cooperation, create new research opportunities and deepen their strategic partnership. Horizon Europe currently includes 23 associated non-EU countries, ranging from the United Kingdom, Canada, and Japan to South Korea and Switzerland. The association will enable Indian institutions to receive grants directly from the European Commission and allow Indian scientists to lead and coordinate major international research projects, on terms similar to those available to organisations in EU member states, in the covered areas. The agreement is expected to give a fresh impetus to India-EU scientific and technological cooperation and strengthen collaboration in emerging technologies and innovation. Rishu Jaiswal, Akashvani News, Delhi.”

The National Health Authority, under the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare reviewed the progress of two flagship healthcare initiatives, Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY), and the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM). It focused on expanding beneficiary coverage, improving healthcare delivery, strengthening financial protection and accelerating the adoption of digital health services. The two-day National Review Meeting which concluded in Kolkata yesterday, brought together senior officials from States and Union Territories to assess the progress of both schemes and discuss priorities for their next phase of implementation.
The discussions also highlighted the role of technology, data analytics, automation and Artificial Intelligence in improving operational efficiency, transparency and accountability, as well as healthcare outcomes. Addressing the meeting, National Health Authority Chief Executive Officer Dr. Sunil Kumar Barnwal said the next phase of implementation must go beyond expanding coverage and focus on ensuring better-quality healthcare for beneficiaries.

The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has issued guidelines to standardise the design and infrastructure of toll plazas on four-lane and wider National Highways. In a statement, Road Transport and Highways Ministry said, the guidelines will ensure that upcoming and ongoing National Highway projects are equipped to support Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF)-based barrier-free toll collection, allowing vehicles to pass through toll plazas without stopping.

 Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh is set to celebrate the 10th edition of Deepotsav today, with more than 30 lakh earthen lamps set to illuminate the holy city on the eve of festival of lights, Diwali. Vice President CP Radhakrishnan will attend the celebrations. During his visit, he will offer prayers at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple, participate in the symbolic coronation ceremony of Prabhu Shri Ram and felicitate revered saints.

 

“A ceremonial procession will be taken out from Saket Mahavidyalaya at 10 AM, which will be flagged off by Uttar Pradesh Tourism Minister Jaiveer Singh. More than 30 lakh earthen lamps have been laid at Ram Ki Paidi, the main venue of the celebrations, with the help of over 35,000 volunteers. The counting of the lamps was completed yesterday, and the process of filling them with oil and placing wicks will begin this morning. Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan will attend the celebrations as the chief guest. Governor Anandiben Patel, ambassadors from several countries and other distinguished guests will also be present. SUSHIL CHANDRA TIWARI AKASHVANI NEWS LUCKNOW.”

 The Ministry of Railways has stepped up preparations to manage the heavy passenger rush during the Diwali and Chhath festivals. As part of its crowd-management measures, the Railways is operating 18,000 special trains, deploying additional Railway Protection Force personnel and installing Artificial Intelligence-enabled cameras at major railway stations. Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw stated this while inspecting the passenger holding areas at New Delhi Railway Station last evening. Mr. Vaishnaw said, New Delhi Railway Station handles over five lakh passengers on an average day, while the daily footfall rises to around eight lakh during peak periods.

 

Mr. Vaishnaw further said that more than 700 Artificial Intelligence-enabled cameras have been installed at New Delhi Railway Station to monitor passenger movement and ensure effective crowd management.

The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has released the date sheet for the Class 10th and Class 12th board examinations 2027. The examinations for both classes will begin on the 16th of February next year, with papers commencing at 10:30 AM. According to the official timetable, the Class 10 examinations will conclude on the 9th of March, while the Class 12 examinations will continue until the 9th of April. As per the notification, Class 10 students will appear in examinations for 83 subjects, while Class 12 students will take examinations in 121 subjects. The Board said the date sheet was prepared after carefully considering more than 40 thousand subject combinations to ensure that students do not face any clash between examinations of the subjects they have opted for.

The security situation in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir has further deteriorated after Pakistani security forces launched an operation against protesters in Rawalakot leaving several civilians dead and scores injured. Violence erupted near Umar Farooq Chowk after security personnel moved to dismantle a protest camp set up by the Joint Awami Action Committee, which has been leading a prolonged agitation over political and economic demands. According to media reports, security forces opened fire on protesters, resulting in multiple casualties while several protesters sustained injuries.

US President Donald Trump has named Stephen Miller, a key architect of his hardline immigration policies, as the new White House Chief of Staff. The appointment follows major losses for the Republican Party in the US midterm elections, which resulted in the party losing control of both chambers of Congress. Miller will replace Susie Wiles, who has stepped down from the position. President Trump praised her work, saying she had done a very good job, but added that changes were sometimes necessary.

In Jammu and Kashmir, the Meteorological Department has forecast generally dry weather across the Union Territory till the 9th of November, with light rain and snowfall over higher reaches likely from 10th of this month. According to the latest weather advisory, light rain is expected at scattered to many places on 10th and 11th of November, while higher reaches may receive light snowfall.

In a major overhaul of Agnipath scheme, the Union Cabinet has approved a revised framework creating a pathway for 100 percent absorption of all willing Agniveers into the Defence Forces. Briefing media after the Cabinet meeting, Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani said, the move follows an extensive evaluation by the armed forces that gave highly positive feedback on Agniveer efficacy, physical fitness, and technological adaptability.

 

The decision comes just before the first batch of 18,300 Agniveers completes its initial four-year tenure next month.

 

“As originally planned, the top 25% of Agniveers will be offered regular permanent employment immediately after their initial 4-year tenure based on merit. The remaining 75% of Agniveers will now be given an additional engagement period of two years, subject to candidate willingness and recommendations from the forces.

 

Upon finishing the additional two-year extension (bringing total service to 6 years), all remaining willing Agniveers will be offered permanent enrolment as regular soldiers, provided they meet standard selection criteria.

The newly added two-year extension period will feature increased monthly remuneration, an enhanced Seva Nidhi package, and cumulative seniority benefits.

 

The structural reforms effectively remove the mandatory 75% exit provision, ensuring that any Agniveer who wishes to serve permanently and meets the benchmark criteria will have a direct route to do so. YASHASVI KIRYAL, for Akashvani News, DELHI.”

Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, to provide for immediate suspension of manufacturing licences in respect of drugs declared Not of Standard Quality on specified critical quality parameters. The proposed amendments seek to enable prompt regulatory intervention upon detection of substandard medicines, prevent their continued manufacture and distribution, and strengthen the mechanism for ensuring compliance in the interest of patient safety and public health.

 

“The Health Ministry said that under the existing provisions, suspension or cancellation of a manufacturing licence is preceded by the prescribed regulatory procedure, including issuance of a show-cause notice. The Ministry added that the proposed amendment also provides for mandatory corrective measures before revocation of the suspension. The suspension shall continue until the manufacturer undertakes an effective Root Cause Analysis and implements appropriate Corrective and Preventive Action to the satisfaction of the concerned Licensing Authority. The Ministry said that the amendments are expected to strengthen post-marketing regulatory surveillance, facilitate timely action against substandard medicines, promote greater accountability among manufacturers and marketers. The draft amendments have been notified for public consultation and  objections and suggestions have been invited  from stakeholders and members of the public within 30 days. With ANAND KUMAR, SHIVANG MISRA, AKASHVANI NEWS, DELHI.”

The government has notified a new set of rules governing India’s civil aviation sector, replacing the nearly nine-decade-old Aircraft Rules, 1937. The new rules called the Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2026, will come into effect on 1st of January, next year. The rules provide the regulatory framework on various aspects of the aviation sector including aircraft registration, manufacturing, safety certification, maintenance, flight operations, personnel licensing and airport operations.

 

Airlines operating scheduled air services are required to determine fares based on factors such as operating costs and submit tariff details to the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA). The provision allows the Centre to issue written directions if it determines that an extraordinary situation has arisen and intervention is necessary in the public interest. The new rules also mandate greater transparency in airfare pricing, requiring airlines to publish their fares on official websites and other digital platforms. The DGCA will continue to monitor tariffs set by scheduled airlines. One of the key areas covered by the rules is the registration and certification of aircraft. They specify requirements for registering aircraft in India and obtaining certificates that establish whether an aircraft is safe to fly.

The Election Commission of India (ECI) has reviewed preparations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections in 18 districts across four divisions and directed senior officials to strengthen voter lists, security arrangements and personnel training to ensure free, fair and peaceful polling.

The review meeting was chaired by Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Manish Garg in Meerut in the presence of Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Navdeep Rinwa and other senior commission officials, according to a statement issued by the CEO’s office.

 

Mr Garg emphasised the importance of the review for both first-time district election officers and police chiefs and experienced officials, noting that election rules and guidelines undergo periodic changes. He urged all officials to examine the issues discussed afresh and improve their preparations accordingly.

 

He also stressed ensuring minimum assured facilities at polling stations and launching EVM awareness programmes. The senior deputy election commissioner instructed authorities to maintain strict surveillance against the illegal transportation and distribution of liquor during the elections, including checks at distilleries’ source and exit points.

 

He also called for effective arrangements for mobile phone deposit boxes at polling stations on polling day, with the assistance of volunteers. Officials were asked to ensure training for state-level master trainers and familiarise relevant personnel with postal ballot-related instructions.

 

Rinwa directed officials to launch special drives in classes 11 and 12 and degree colleges to enrol young people becoming eligible to vote for the first time. He also asked authorities to re-examine rejected Form 6 applications to ensure that eligible citizens are included in electoral rolls.

 

Applicants filling Form 6 should provide their mobile numbers and complete addresses accurately, while Common Service Centre operators should be trained immediately in the online application process and measures to prevent multiple entries. The CEO further directed district election officers to recheck all Forms 6, 7 and 8 entered by computer assistants since the conclusion of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The CEO also directed officials to ensure distribution of voter information slips five days before polling and record the distribution in booth-level officers’ registers.
